trigger: Breach of security (unauthorized access of electronic data containing personal information) of Florida residents: name with SSN, driver license, passport, or similar ID number, among the 501.171(1)(g) elements. Encrypted data is excluded
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred; 15 more days only if good cause for delay is given in writing to the Department of Legal Affairs within the 30 days (501.171(3)(a))
notify: Each affected Florida individual by mail or email (date or date range, information involved, and a contact at the business)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - 66 Floridians have an SSN or ID number in the mailbox today; recount from the actual mailbox and ATS export

obligation: Florida no-harm determination (alternative to individual notice)
trigger: After an appropriate investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the business reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept at least 5 years and provided to the Department of Legal Affairs within 30 days after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Only if counsel supports it; unlikely once an attacker has searched a mailbox holding SSNs

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (no extension for this notice)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely - 66 Floridians in the mailbox; recount if the ATS export held ID images for more people

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely - most of the 3,400 ATS records hold no 501.171(1)(g) element

trigger: A law enforcement agency determines that notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period in the agency's written request
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the business (inbound)
trigger: The email provider, ATS vendor, or another vendor that maintains personal information for the business has a breach of its system
deadline: Vendor must notify the business as expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after determination; the business then gives notices under (3) and (4)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - register the owner as breach contact with each vendor

trigger: Affected people who live outside Florida (11 people in 6 other states are in the mailbox today)
notify: Residents and regulators under the law of each state where affected individuals reside
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - check the residence state of every affected person; counsel confirms each state's trigger and deadline

obligation: Partner notice of suspected payroll diversion
trigger: Any sign that the attacker contacted the partner or a bank-change request came from the owner's mailbox
deadline: Immediately by phone, before the next pay date
notify: Partner payroll desk and account manager
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual and practical; the partner is the employer and decides any notice to its employees

obligation: Client notice of a security incident
trigger: Incident affecting client information (job orders, client contacts, submittals)
deadline: Promptly (fee agreements give no fixed number of hours)
notify: Client hiring contacts in the fee agreement
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if client information was in the mailbox or ATS export

trigger: Suspected security incident or funds transfer fraud
applies_at_this_tier: Only if coverage exists - no standalone cyber policy; ask the professional liability carrier about a cyber endorsement before hiring outside firms

trigger: Business email compromise or attempted payroll diversion
deadline: As soon as possible (supports recovery of diverted funds and any 501.171(4)(b) delay request)

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: An extortion demand is received and payment is considered
deadline: Before any payment; reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor

citation: E-Verify MOU for Employers Art. II.A.16
trigger: Loss of control of E-Verify personal data
applies_at_this_tier: No - the business is not an E-Verify participant; the partner runs E-Verify for contractors

trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI held for a covered entity
deadline: No later than 60 calendar days after discovery
applies_at_this_tier: No - the business is not a business associate (P03 G-117)

obligation: CIRCIA incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed only: 72 hours; 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; recheck when final

trigger: Covered article identified while performing a federal contract
deadline: Within 1 business day for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases
applies_at_this_tier: No - the business holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
